style: A single medieval building seen from a high three-quarter isometric angle, in the hand-painted style of Crusader Kings III's domicile buildings: clean dark ink outlines, soft watercolour shading, muted earthy palette, warm stone and timber, a small patch of ground at its base, no people, no text, no border, isolated on a plain transparent background.

regions.western: Romanesque northern European town architecture of the 11th-13th centuries: grey and ochre stone, steep red-tile or slate roofs, round arches, timber framing (Rhineland, northern France, England).
regions.mena: Mediterranean and Islamic-world town architecture of the 10th-13th centuries: whitewashed or sandstone walls, flat roofs and low domes, horseshoe or pointed arches, courtyards, palms (al-Andalus, Egypt, the Levant, Byzantium).

families.synagogue: a medieval synagogue: a tall prayer hall with round-arched windows and a small rose window, a modest gable, steps to a single door; no Christian or Islamic symbols, no star.
families.beit_midrash: a house of study attached to a small courtyard: a long hall with many windows and benches visible through an open door, books on shelves.
families.kahal_house: a dignified two-storey council house of a Jewish community, with an arcade on the ground floor and a meeting hall above.
families.hekdesh: a communal poorhouse and hospice: a plain long building with a courtyard, a well, and beds visible through an open shutter.
families.kosher_market: a small covered market of butchers' and bakers' stalls with awnings, a wine cask and hanging meat, under an arcade.
families.craft_row: a short street of craftsmen's workshops with open shopfronts: dye vats, a loom, a goldsmith's bench.
families.bankers_row: a prosperous stone townhouse with a moneychanger's counter and scales at an open window, a strongbox inside.
families.funduq: a funduq, a merchants' courtyard inn and warehouse: two storeys of rooms around a courtyard, bales and sacks, a laden mule.
families.wall_and_gates: a fortified gate of a walled town quarter: two squat towers with crenellations, an arched gateway with a heavy wooden gate, a short stretch of wall.
